sink_file: assets/lib/fuc.js.php  (the fetch_url_contents js->php URL proxy; ?url= is fetched server-side)
incomplete_fix_quote: This is a Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. It exists in /assets/lib/fuc.js.php and allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files or send TCP traffic to intranet hosts via the url parameter. It stems from an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-14611.
root_cause: fuc.js.php proxies $_REQUEST['url'] to curl (FOLLOWLOCATION on) and returns the body. The CVE-2017-14611 fix (commit 0711d4f9) added filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_URL) + a preg_match('#^http(|s)\://#') scheme allow-list. It restricts the URL SCHEME (blocking file://, gopher://, dict://) but NOT the DESTINATION, so an http:// URL aimed at an internal-only host still passes the guard and is fetched server-side -> SSRF to intranet hosts. That residual is CVE-2018-9302.

patch_refs.v0_to_v1_14611_fix: agentejo/cockpit commit 0711d4f9 'Fix possible vulnerability in window.fetch_url_contents' (2017-09-20), assets/lib/fuc.js.php (see patch.diff)
patch_refs.note_on_v2: commit e028770c (2018-05-07, 'minor improvements') only hardened the missing-HTTP_HOST case and did NOT close the http-SSRF; upstream did not ship a clean scheme-independent destination filter for this proxy in a single following commit, so no V2 profile is provided.

version_pins.v0: commit a5fb51cb (parent of the 14611 fix; no scheme guard)

libcurl_note: The published PoC bounces off an attacker open-redirect to re-reach non-http schemes (gopher/dict/file). On modern libcurl (>=7.19.4) CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS excludes file:// so a redirect->file local read is not client-followable (verified empirically on libcurl 7.64.0). The direct http:// intranet SSRF is the minimal, deterministic residual and is what this case gates on.
